newsitem.title: UK: BRENT FIRMS AND FADES BUT OTHER NSEA GRADES HOLD UP.
newsitem.headline: BRENT FIRMS AND FADES BUT OTHER NSEA GRADES HOLD UP.

text.p: Dated Brent firmed and then drifted off on Tuesday, dragging paper through the same twists, while other North Sea crudes were stronger, traders said.

A wet Brent trade at Sept -15 cents to a U.S. major caused some surprise among players who thought the market's recent falls were continuing and who were offering similarly dated Brent at lower numbers.
A second Brent deal later redressed some of the balance. The Aug 20-22 cargo moved between traders at Sept -20 cents, the same value that it achieved last Thursday.
Intermonth spreads firmed with Sept/Oct trading at -13 cents, -11 cents and -12 cents.
Short-term swaps also rose on the stronger Brent deal before the second benchmark cargo deal knocked off some of the gain.
"Initially the CFDs (contracts for differences) were looking really strong but after the second Brent they came off again," said one dealer.

Next week's CFDs (Aug 18-22) ended being offered at Oct -20 cents, up 10 cents, while the following week (Aug 25-29) gained the same amount to be offered at Oct -21 cents. Sept 1-5 traded at Oct -25 cents and Sept 8-12 at Oct -22 cts.

Underlying demand for the remaining August Brent cargoes was said by some to be good, with reports of shorts into the U.S. Gulf and Poland. Both of today's dates were kept, one by BP, the other by J.Aron.
Technicals and strong U.S. gasoline helped IPE Brent to gain 19 cents to $18.77 a barrel by 1730 gmt and non-Brent North Sea crudes saw differentials tick upwards on fears of near-term tightness.
Traders discounted the two Statfjord deals at Brent +5 and +4 on Monday as done for tax spinning purpose and pegged offer levels for the grade at +25 cents.
Supply worries were underlined by reports production problems at the Snorre field have delayed all loadings of Statfjord cargoes by two days, the second deferral for the August programme.

Two Forties cargoes were traded on Tuesday on a private basis but traders believed the prices to be a slightly stronger 30 to 35 cents above Dated Brent. Earlier an end-month Troll traded at dated Brent +21 cents.
"Overall the market looks a bit more constructive," said one trader, "it definetly feels a bit stronger."
Osebergs were pegged at +0.15/0.25 with business in limbo while traders awaited the results of the Lagoven tender for which they had offered.
